question: Did Jesus have a real human body, or only seem to?

answers.label: He had real flesh, suffered and rose in it
He only seemed to have a body and to suffer

overview.text: Some early teachers said Christ only seemed to suffer. The bishops who answered them were the earliest generation after the apostles: Ignatius about 110 and Polycarp about 135.
They insisted on real flesh at every step: born, crucified, raised, eating with his disciples after the resurrection. Tertullian pressed the same point against Marcion.

quotes.author: Docetists, as Ignatius reports
quotes.context: The view Ignatius answers, in the three words he quotes from its teachers.

quotes.author: Ignatius of Antioch
quotes.english: But if, as some who are godless, that is, unbelievers, say, he only seemed to suffer (they themselves only seem to exist!), why am I in chains? Why do I pray to fight the wild beasts? Then I die for nothing. Then I am lying about the Lord.
quotes.original: Εἰ δέ, ὥσπερ τινὲς ἄθεοι ὄντες, τουτέστιν ἄπιστοι, λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν πεπονθέναι αὐτόν, αὐτοὶ ὄντες τὸ δοκεῖν, ἐγὼ τί δέδεμαι, τί δὲ καὶ εὔχομαι θηριομαχῆσαι; δωρεὰν οὖν ἀποθνήσκω. ἄρα οὖν καταψεύδομαι τοῦ κυρίου.
quotes.context: "Seemed" (dokein) gave these teachers their name, Docetists. Ignatius stakes his own martyrdom on Christ's real suffering.

quotes.author: Ignatius of Antioch
quotes.english: I know and believe that even after the resurrection he was in the flesh. And when he came to Peter and those with him, he said to them: "Take, handle me and see that I am not a bodiless ghost" (compare Luke 24:39). And at once they touched him and believed, being joined with his flesh and spirit. ... After the resurrection he ate and drank with them as one in the flesh, though spiritually united with the Father.
quotes.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτὸν οἶδα καὶ πιστεύω ὄντα. καὶ ὅτε πρὸς τοὺς περὶ Πέτρον ἦλθεν, ἔφη αὐτοῖς: Λάβετε, ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον. καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτοῦ ἥψαντο καὶ ἐπίστευσαν, κραθέντες τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι. ... μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάστασιν συνέφαγεν αὐτοῖς καὶ συνέπιεν ὡς σαρκικός, καίπερ πνευματικῶς ἡνωμένος
quotes.context: Written against the Docetists at Smyrna.

quotes.author: Polycarp of Smyrna
quotes.english: Everyone who does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is antichrist (1 John 4:2–3); and whoever does not confess the testimony of the cross is of the devil; and whoever twists the Lord's sayings to suit his own desires and says there is neither resurrection nor judgment, that one is the firstborn of Satan.
quotes.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν μὴ ὁμολογῇ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθέναι, ἀντιχριστός ἐστιν: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ὁμολογῇ τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν: καὶ ὃς ἂν μεθοδεύῃ τὰ λόγια τοῦ κυρίου πρὸς τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας καὶ λέγῃ μήτε ἀνάστασιν μήτε κρίσιν, οὗτος πρωτότοκος ἐστι τοῦ σατανᾶ.
quotes.context: Polycarp, a disciple of John according to Irenaeus, quotes 1 John against the same teachers.

quotes.author: Serapion of Antioch
quotes.work: Letter on the Gospel of Peter, quoted by Eusebius in Church History
quotes.english: We, brethren, receive Peter and the other apostles as Christ, but as men of experience we reject what is falsely written under their names, since we know that we did not receive such things. ... We were able, with the help of others who had practiced this gospel itself, that is, of the successors of those who began it, whom we call Docetists, to go through it, and to find most of it of the right word of the Saviour, but some things added apart.
quotes.original: ἡμεῖς γὰρ, ἀδελφοί, καὶ Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους ἀποστόλους ἀποδεχόμεθα ὡς Χριστόν, τὰ δὲ ὀνόματι αὐτῶν ψευδεπίγραφα ὡς ἔμπειροι παραιτούμεθα, γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὰ τοιαῦτα οὐ παρελάβομεν. ... ἐδυνήθημεν γὰρ παρ᾽ ἄλλων τῶν ἀσκησάντων αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, τουτέστι παρὰ τῶν διαδόχων τῶν καταρξαμένων αὐτοῦ, οὓς Δοκητὰς καλοῦμεν
quotes.context: Serapion's own words, surviving only as quoted by Eusebius from his letter to the church at Rhossus. He had allowed the Gospel of Peter to be read there, then borrowed a copy from the successors of the people who began it, whom he names the Docetists, read it through, and found most of it sound but some things interpolated.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: The Son of God was crucified: I am not ashamed, because it is shameful. The Son of God died: it is wholly believable, because it is absurd. He was buried and rose again: it is certain, because it is impossible. For how will these things be true in him if he himself was not true, if he did not truly have in himself what could be nailed, could die, could be buried and raised: this flesh, filled with blood, built on bones?
quotes.original: Crucifixus est dei filius; non pudet, quia pudendum est. Et mortuus est dei filius; prorsus credibile est, quia ineptum est. Et sepultus resurresit; certum est, quia impossibile est. Nam quomodo vera in illo erunt, si ipse non fuit verus, si non vere habuit in se quod figeretur, quod moreretur, quod sepeliretur et resuscitaretur? carnem scilicet hanc sanguine suffusam, ossibus
quotes.context: The source of the misquote "I believe because it is absurd". Tertullian is arguing against Marcion that Christ's flesh was real.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
